result:
I've written round 424 as the fix-up for the one bug C found in round 423. The decision in `b-next.json` is **CONTINUE**.

**Round 423 result (taken from C's evidence only).** C failed the round on one Medium bug, C-R423-01. Every other row passed (21 of 22), and `browserVerified` is true. The root gate skipped the round, so the baseline stays `875ff37`. I did not update `regression-last.json`, because part 2 of the regression hasn't run yet. The round-423 task is archived byte-identical as `tasks/round-423.md`.

**The bug.** 17 fixed perf budgets for clip drags fail. Each drag now re-renders the lane component three times per update instead of once:
- fade 6 against a budget of 4;
- trim 17 against 15;
- each video drag 2 over its budget.

I found the cause with a browser probe that names each re-rendered component, before handing anything to A. Round 409 split the Lane into an outer wrapper plus a memoised inner part, and the wrapper now re-renders on every drag update. That round never ran the perf suite, so I logged the bug as a planning (B) defect. Drag latency is unchanged (every p95 ≤ 7.8 ms), so users can't feel this; the budgets exist to catch exactly this kind of regression.

**Ruling: fix the code, keep the budgets.**
- tech-lead recommended the fix.
- performance-optimizer recommended raising the budgets by 2 instead. I recorded that dissent and its idea of a drag-latency budget as an unscheduled candidate.
- The fix moves the drag-time data subscriptions into the memoised inner part, so a drag update renders the lane once.
- The sketch changes 2 files: `ArrangementLane.tsx` and four rows in `drag-preview-render.test.tsx`, which now also check that the outer wrapper renders 0 times.
- tech-lead reviewed the sketch and approved it with four minor findings. Three went to the deferred low-priority list, and the fourth isn't a defect.

**Checks I ran on the sketch:**
- **Perf:** the whole suite passes (5 specs, 19.1 min). All 17 budgets are back at their round-404 values, and no component count got worse.
- **Browser probes:** fade 6 → 4, trim 17 → 15, and the outer wrapper renders 0 times during a drag. The lane, leaf-actions, video-sync and cross-lane ghost-title probes match HEAD apart from wallclock timing.
- **Tests:** 3,957/3,957 in the full suite; typecheck and lint pass.
- **Mutant:** the old Lane code with the new test rows turns exactly 4 rows red.

**Still above round 404 after the fix** (recorded as `INFO-B423-LANE-RESTORE-PARTIAL`): zoom 41 → 45, and the largest move/lane and group commits +4. None of these has a budget, or each is within it. Round 409's own saving survives: play start/stop renders dropped from 11 to 7.

The close-of-planning advisor review found seven gaps in the task. All are fixed, which is why I ran the whole perf suite and the browser probes on the sketch rather than citing round 423's numbers.

**Order after this round:** round 425 is regression part 2, then STEM-LANES once Saba answers `AGREE-STEM-LANES.md` (still unanswered), otherwise SYS-2 stage 2a. The backlog is at v400 (D-29z1479…D-29z1482).

Nothing in `store/` changed: the sketch work ran in a scratch copy under `/tmp`, and its dev server ran on its own port and was stopped afterwards. Everything else is under `tmp/studio-real-loop/`. Open `current-task.md` and `b-round-423.md` first; the evidence is in `b-round-423/`.
